learned: Breville's own Extraction Guide uses 'bitter' for both failure modes. On both machines the under-extraction column says a fast shot 'Tastes bitter/sharp, weak and watery', and over-extraction is 'bitter and burnt'. Only the summary table ties under-extraction to 'Underdeveloped • Sour'. Flow start, shot time and the gauge or shot clock separate the two more reliably than the taste words (barista-express/extraction-guide-over-and-summary, barista-pro/extraction-guide-over-and-summary).

On the Express, the gauge is meant as a diagnostic. The Extraction Guide pairs a correct shot with the needle 'Within Espresso Range', a fast shot with 'Under Espresso Range' and a choked shot with 'Over Espresso Range'. No bar values are given (barista-express/pressure-gauge-zones).

The Barista Pro has no pressure gauge. Owners diagnose with the LCD shot clock, which counts up from pre-infusion, and with flow start: 8–12 s is right, under 7 s means under-extracted, no flow after 13 s means over-extracted (barista-pro/no-pressure-gauge-lcd-shot-clock, barista-pro/extraction-guide-fast-shot).

The Express booklet contradicts itself on flow start: page 18 says 4–7 s and page 20 says 8–12 s. The only single target it gives is a total shot time of 25–30 s, with under 20 s meaning under-extracted (barista-express/flow-start-figures-differ, barista-express/dose-and-extraction-targets).

Neither machine doses by weight. The Express GRIND AMOUNT dial starts at 3 o'clock and is checked by the tamper-cap level. The Pro's GRIND AMOUNT is a grind time, 9.5 s single and 13 s double by default. Breville says a finer grind in single-wall baskets may need a larger grind amount, and that switching baskets means re-adjusting both grind size and grind amount. Grinding finer without raising the dose leaves the basket under-filled (barista-express/grind-amount-dial-dosing, barista-pro/grind-amount-time-based, barista-pro/baskets-single-vs-dual-wall).

Breville says to use single-wall baskets with fresh beans. Dual-wall baskets 'regulate the pressure' regardless of grind, dose or tamp, so dialing in in a dual-wall basket hides the real variables. The Pro ships with the 2-cup single-wall basket installed (barista-express/baskets-single-vs-dual-wall, barista-pro/single-wall-2cup-installed).

1 CUP and 2 CUP stop at a preset volume of about 30 ml and 60 ml, not at a weight or time. Breville notes that the output varies with grind size and grind amount. Holding the button runs a manual shot: pre-infusion while held, full pressure on release, press again to stop. On the Express, holding PROGRAM until 3 beeps resets both the volumes and the default temperature (barista-express/shot-volume-preset-program-manual, barista-pro/shot-volume-preset-program-manual).

Temperature is a late, small lever. The Express offers ±4°F in 2°F steps through Advanced Temperature Mode, and the Pro has a SHOT TEMP menu with no stated range. Breville also warns that a cold portafilter and basket can reduce extraction temperature 'enough to significantly affect the quality', and says to wipe the basket dry because moisture encourages channeling (barista-express/temperature-adjust-2f-steps, barista-pro/shot-temp-adjustable, barista-express/preheat-and-dry-basket).

Bean freshness is in Breville's own list: use beans with a 'Roasted On' date and use them 5–20 days after roasting. The Pro booklet says stale coffee 'may pour too quickly' and taste 'bitter and watery' (barista-pro/beans-roasted-on-5-20-days, barista-express/beans-roasted-on-5-20-days).

Breville's troubleshooting tables attribute fast shots and no crema only to grind, dose, tamp, freshness, a blocked basket and basket choice. The only row on either machine that sends the owner to Breville support is the thermal cut-out row ('Machine is on but ceases to operate') (barista-express/troubleshooting-only-thermal-cutout-to-support, barista-pro/troubleshooting-only-thermal-cutout-to-support, barista-express/troubleshooting-runs-too-quickly).

Owner pattern: a new Express owner thought the gauge was broken. It moved once they ground at setting 1–2, filled the basket higher and tamped harder, and they kept the machine, calling it 'finicky about the dose' (barista-express/owner-gauge-not-moving-was-dose).

Owner pattern: an owner at grind 1–3 getting 20 g in and 20–27 g out in 15–20 s got split advice in the replies: overfilled basket or channeling, the inner burr, single- vs dual-wall baskets, temperature. Another owner found that grinding finer made the shot more sour until they raised the temperature and learned that program and manual modes differ (barista-express/owner-fast-shots-split-advice, barista-express/owner-sour-finer-more-sour).

When the outer dial runs out, Breville documents the upper (inner) burr as an owner adjustment, one number at a time (barista-express/upper-burr-adjustment-documented, barista-pro/upper-burr-adjustment-documented).
unknowns: No Breville or Sage source documents a test that separates a real pressure fault (pump, OPV, gauge) from a dial-in problem, for example the expected gauge reading with a dual-wall basket. The writer can only say to contact support after the documented checks fail. Breville support should be asked directly (barista-express/machine-fault-test-not-documented, barista-pro/machine-fault-test-not-documented). The Home-Barista low-pressure thread returned 403.
The gauge zones have no bar values in the X26 booklet. Third-party guides say 8–10 bar or that the gauge reads high, but these were not traced to Breville.

The GB variants (Sage SES875, SES878) were not checked for the same Extraction Guide, gauge zones and flow-start figures. All new claims are scoped to the US variants. Add to the library: the current Sage UK full instruction booklets for SES875 and SES878.

The Barista Express Impress (BES876) is in the audience but has no card. Its dosing is different (assisted tamp, dose dial), so the dose steps may not apply. Add to the library: https://assets.breville.com/BES876/BES876_ANZ_IB_QA_C22_WEB.pdf and a US BES876 booklet.

The Express booklet doesn't say what the GRIND AMOUNT dial positions mean in seconds or grams. The program-versus-manual difference the Lemmy owner mentions is not explained beyond volumetric presets versus press-and-hold.

Add to the library: https://assets.breville.com/BES870/BES870_USCM_IB_X26_LR.pdf and https://assets.breville.com/BES878/BES878_USCM_IB_Q26_LR.pdf. This run read them as page images, and WebFetch could not extract their text.

competitors.says: This is a first-time setup and dial-in guide for the Express, not a fault-finder. It doesn't treat a gauge that won't move as a diagnostic, and it doesn't flag that Breville's own guide calls a fast shot 'bitter/sharp'. Assessed from the search result and the idea card; the full page was not fetched this run.

'10 common problems' listicle. Its search snippet describes the right symptom: 'gushes out too fast, gauge barely moves... sour and watery'. It also claims the gauge reads high because the OPV is set above 9 bar, which is not traced to Breville. Not fetched in full.

A forum thread, typical of what ranks: owners argue that the gauge mostly tracks grind coarseness and should be ignored. Advice is scattered over many posts and there's no ordered checklist. Assessed from the search result only.

cardChanges.summary: Added sour/bitter diagnosis claims from the X26 booklet: gauge zones, the over-extraction column and summary table (including the booklet's use of 'bitter' for both failure modes), the conflicting flow-start figures, grind-amount dosing, preset versus manual shot volume, preheating, and the troubleshooting rows that point to support. Added three owner-report claims (OzBargain x2, Lemmy) and an unknown claim for a manufacturer fault test. No existing claims were removed.
